A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EW-DETR research and contain complete main texts and appendices. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original Pascal Series and Diverse Weather experiments, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds component controls, query-norm measurements, and unknown-class sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The incremental LoRA merging procedure, QNorm-Obj, EUMix, and training objectives remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A. Added ablation variants and implementation disclosures do not establish a changed proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Pascal and Diverse Weather datasets, domains, and detection tasks. V2's alternative withheld-class assignments are split variants within existing coverage, rather than new datasets or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds simple task-adapter PEFT, jointly trained dual LoRA without merging/SVD, and QNorm-Obj-only controls. The external comparator set in the main benchmark comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds controlled training configurations, three alternative unknown-class splits, and matched/unmatched query evaluation using ROC-AUC. Its implementation section changes rank from 8 to 16, resolving a conflict with v1's sensitivity section, which already specified 16; this does not establish rerunning existing experiments.

E4.justification: Validation expands substantially: Table 4 tests alternatives to the proposed adapter mechanism and QNorm-Obj alone; new Appendix C directly examines the norm-objectness premise; Appendix G.2 tests dependence on the withheld unknown category. These address distinct mechanism and robustness questions beyond v1's existing analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations across sensitivity configurations. V2 expands the configurations and updates dispersion values but introduces no new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores remain unchanged. New Table 4 controls report FOGS 37.40, 37.16, and 31.14; new unknown-class splits report 53.17–53.76 in Table S5. Figure S2 adds query-norm measurements and ROC-AUC 0.585/0.587. Table S5 also changes dispersion values; these are additional results, not improved retained scores.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, adapter equations, EUMix formulation, and FOGS definitions are retained. Added explanations of temperature, numerical stability, and merging bounds do not introduce new mathematical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same EWOD paradigm, three-module framework, FOGS contribution, and claimed 57.24% improvement. Added evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets query norms as a persistent objectness signal and the new withheld-class tests as evidence against dependence on a particular unknown category. Appendix G.1 also newly discusses six-layer detector collapse and the rationale for using one layer. The existing generalisation limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix F corrects the rank inconsistency and newly describes baseline adaptation, including EBUI for DuET. Appendix G.1 discloses the single-layer Deformable DETR setting. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the retained experiments; optimisation budgets and hardware remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to CL-LoRA, SD-LoRA, and Zero-shot Generalizable Incremental Learning for Vision-Language Object Detection. It adds targeted contrasts concerning data-aware merging and auxiliary supervision, while retaining the broader research positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose remains unchanged. V2 adds a query-norm appendix subsection and localized explanations, moves sensitivity discussions ahead of comprehensive results, updates appendix references, and corrects the t-SNE reference from Figure S3 to Figure 4.

P2.justification: V2 adds the query-norm histogram, expands Table 4 and the sensitivity table, and groups existing qualitative, summary, and hyperparameter figures on the final page. Existing principal illustrations and overall visual design are retained.

improvement.justification: The added controls and mechanism/robustness analyses strengthen support for the existing method, while the rank correction and baseline disclosures improve reproducibility. These are useful but bounded gains. Variability reporting remains unclear: Appendix G.2 quotes OSS/FOGS standard deviations of 1.11/1.26, whereas expanded Table S5 reports 1.39/1.65 without clearly distinguishing the aggregation.
